Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We document \emph{universal GRPO reward-accuracy decoupling}: reward improvement never translates to accuracy gain post-SFT, and this holds bidirectionally---neither reward increase on unpruned models nor reward collapse on pruned models changes reasoning performance.
    \item We identify \emph{pruning-induced GRPO training collapse} with a severity gradient that diagnoses structural damage type: CKA-aware pruning (\rasp{}) collapses 6$\times$ faster than importance-only pruning at matched sparsity, because it removes the functionally redundant structures that GRPO relies on for stable exploration.
    \item We reveal the \emph{Redundancy-Stability Tradeoff}: structures optimal for SFT recovery (high-overlap, functionally redundant) are exactly those required for RLVR training stability---optimal pruning is fundamentally conditioned on the recovery paradigm.

\end{enumerate}

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item We demonstrate \emph{universal reward-accuracy decoupling} under GRPO: reward improves dramatically on unpruned models yet reasoning accuracy never changes, and this holds bidirectionally---reward collapse on pruned models equally leaves accuracy unchanged.
    \item We show that structural pruning induces \emph{GRPO training collapse}, with severity proportional to redundancy removal: CKA-aware pruning collapses 6$\times$ faster than importance-only pruning at matched sparsity, providing a zero-cost diagnostic of structural damage type.
    \item We reveal a \emph{Redundancy-Stability Tradeoff}: functional redundancy that is safely removable for SFT recovery (+2.2pp) is critical for RLVR training stability---optimal pruning is fundamentally conditioned on the recovery paradigm.
    \item[\textbullet] We introduce \rasp{} as a diagnostic tool whose controlled redundancy removal enables the above analysis.
    \item[\textbullet] [TBD-QwenMath: Multi-model validation contribution.]
\end{enumerate}
